newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Gwalia sees 2nd half below forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Gwalia sees 2nd half below forecasts.

text.p: Gwalia Consolidated Ltd said on Wednesday that its earnings for the second half of the financial year ending June 30 would be below previous forecasts due to increased costs at its Greenbushes tantalite mine.

Gwalia said it now expected to achieve a net profit of between A$8 million and A$10 million in the year to June 30, 1997. It said the problem with some operations meant that its preliminary outlook for 1997/98 would also be affected.
The company said it had not achieved budgeted sales of lithium carbonate in the second half of the current year due to production difficulties.
"Increased global supplies of lithium carbonate from new sources, some at significantly lower than historical prices, has reduced the price and market for the company's lithium carbonate."
Gwalia said it was reviewing its lithium carbonate operations at the Greenbushes mine.
A decision on continuing the operation or placing it on a care-and-maintenance basis would be taken in the near future.
The company, which is the largest shareholder in second-tier gold miner Sons of Gwalia Ltd with a 17.5 percent stake, achieved a 26 percent rise in 1995/96 net profit to A$10.10 million.
